claims.claim: New Zealand has no wealth tax and no general capital gains tax

sources.name: PwC: quick chart, net wealth/worth tax rates
sources.says: Australia (30 June 2026), Japan (07 August 2026), New Zealand (06 July 2026), Singapore (02 July 2026), Taiwan (20 August 2026) and the Republic of Korea (04 June 2026) are all "NA": "the territory does not have the indicated tax".

sources.name: PwC: New Zealand, income determination
sources.says: Last reviewed 06 July 2026. "New Zealand does not have a comprehensive capital gains tax." No FIF income generally where "the total cost of FIF interests held by the individual does not exceed NZD 50,000 at any point in the income year." "The RAM allows qualifying new migrants to calculate FIF income on a realisation basis"; "eligible taxpayers are taxed on dividends received and 70% of any realised gain on disposal of qualifying foreign shares".

claims.claim: New residents get a once-only, roughly 4-year exemption on most foreign income, dividends, interest and FIF income included

sources.name: Inland Revenue: temporary tax exemption
sources.says: Last updated 17 Jun 2026. The exemption "lasts for about 4 years after you become a New Zealand tax resident"; "You can only get the exemption once"; exempt foreign income includes "overseas interest, dividends, foreign investment fund income, rent"; you must not have been tax resident in the 10 years before.

claims.claim: After it, foreign shares and ETFs costing over NZD 50,000 fall under the FIF rules, usually taxed on a deemed 5% of opening market value at up to 39%, or on the actual return in a weaker year, whether or not anything is sold (a yearly charge of up to about 2%)

sources.name: Become: the FIF rules, a plain-English guide
sources.says: Last updated 13 October 2026. The threshold "has been NZ$50,000 since 2000", measured on cost; a bill would double it but "is not law until it passes". FDR "deems 5% of the opening market value ... to be taxable income"; investors can generally use whichever of FDR and CV is lower, and "The minimum taxable income under either method is zero"; FIF applies "regardless of whether gains are realised"; "Tax is paid at your marginal rate up to 39%".

sources.name: PwC: New Zealand, income determination
sources.says: Last reviewed 06 July 2026. "New Zealand does not have a comprehensive capital gains tax." No FIF income generally where "the total cost of FIF interests held by the individual does not exceed NZD 50,000 at any point in the income year." "The RAM allows qualifying new migrants to calculate FIF income on a realisation basis"; "eligible taxpayers are taxed on dividends received and 70% of any realised gain on disposal of qualifying foreign shares".

sources.name: Deloitte: the fifth wave, the FIF reforms continue
sources.says: Dated 22 Sep 2026. The Taxation (Annual Rates for 2026–27, FBT Simplification, Foreign Investment Funds, and Remedial Measures) Bill proposes "the proposed increase of the FIF de minimis threshold from $50,000 to $100,000 with effect from 1 April 2026" and "expanding access to the RAM to all New Zealand-resident individual taxpayers from 1 April 2026".

also: tax fact: added "a bill introduced in September 2026 would raise the FIF threshold to NZD 100,000 and open the revenue account method to all residents" (pending; today's rule scored)
sources: added Deloitte, the fifth wave
claims.note: Searched the FIF threshold bill in November 2026: introduced September 2026, still a proposal in the latest pages read (Become, 13 October 2026), with an election on 7 November 2026 in between. Tax score stays 2 on today's rule.
claims.modelMismatch: localTaxes.ts has no New Zealand entry. The FIF fair-dividend-rate method works like a yearly tax of up to 1.95% of the opening value of foreign shares above NZD 50,000 cost (5% deemed return x 39%), after the 4-year transitional exemption; the revenue account method (US citizens arriving from April 2024) taxes dividends and 70% of realised gains instead.
claims.notModelled: The FIF fair-dividend-rate charge depends on cost (NZD 50,000), the lower of two methods and a 4-year exemption, and qualifying new migrants can use the revenue account method, which taxes a never-sell portfolio only on dividends (outside localTaxes.ts); New Zealand keeps no entry, named with the reason in the localTaxes.ts header.

claims.claim: A US citizen who became resident on or after 1 April 2024, after at least 5 years abroad and once out of the transitional exemption, can opt into the revenue account method (enacted March 2026), taxing dividends and 70% of realised gains

sources.name: Deloitte: a small step, the revenue account method enacted
sources.says: Dated 12 May 2026. Base RAM: individuals who became tax resident on or after 1 April 2024, are not transitional residents, and were non-resident for at least five consecutive years; extended RAM for people taxed because of citizenship, "primarily US citizens and green card holders". Realised gains are discounted by 30% (70% taxable at marginal rates) and dividends remain fully taxable. Introduced by the Taxation (Annual Rates for 2025–26, Compliance Simplification, and Remedial Measures) Act 2026.

sources.name: Inland Revenue (tax policy): compliance simplification Act
sources.says: Published 12 May 2026. The Act "received Royal assent on 30 March 2026."

sources.name: PwC: New Zealand, income determination
sources.says: Last reviewed 06 July 2026. "New Zealand does not have a comprehensive capital gains tax." No FIF income generally where "the total cost of FIF interests held by the individual does not exceed NZD 50,000 at any point in the income year." "The RAM allows qualifying new migrants to calculate FIF income on a realisation basis"; "eligible taxpayers are taxed on dividends received and 70% of any realised gain on disposal of qualifying foreign shares".

claims.note: Deloitte gives the 1 April 2024 and 5-year tests for the base RAM; the extended RAM for US citizens may cover all foreign shares. "(check the exit rules on leaving)" is a hedge.

claims.claim: No inheritance or estate tax (estate duty ended in 1992) and no gift duty since October 2011

sources.name: Inland Revenue (tax technical): gift duty abolition
sources.says: Gift duty is abolished for gifts made "on or after 1 October 2011"; when estate duty was abolished in 1992, gift duty had been kept as a safeguard.

sources.name: PwC: quick chart, inheritance and gift tax rates
sources.says: Inheritance / gift entries: Australia "NA"/"NA" (30 June 2026); Japan 55/55 (07 August 2026); New Zealand "NA"/"NA" (06 July 2026); Singapore "NA"/"NA" (02 July 2026); Taiwan 20/20 (20 August 2026); Republic of Korea 50/50 (04 June 2026). "NA" = "the territory does not have the indicated tax".

sources.name: IRS: Estate & gift tax treaties (international)
sources.says: The table has 15 countries (see us-estate-treaty-list); none of the 37 countries named in this claim is among them.

claims.note: Wording: "there is no US–New Zealand estate tax treaty".

claims.claim: The $15M US estate exemption (2026) applies to a US citizen living here as anywhere

sources.name: IRS: What's new, estate and gift tax
sources.says: The table "Basic exclusion amount for year of death" has the row 2026: $15,000,000 (2025: $13,990,000). The page says the Working Families Tax Cuts, Public Law 119-21, signed July 4, 2025, "amends § 2010(c)(3) by increasing the basic exclusion amount to $15,000,000 for calendar year 2026". Page last reviewed or updated 03-Nov-2026.

sources.name: IRS: Some nonresidents with U.S. assets must file estate tax returns
sources.says: "U.S. citizens are subject to U.S. estate taxation with respect to their worldwide assets"; Form 706 is required when worldwide assets plus adjusted taxable gifts exceed the basic exclusion amount in effect on the date of death. By contrast a nonresident who is not a citizen files when US-situated assets exceed $60,000. Page last reviewed or updated 27-Jun-2026.

claims.note: Wording: "the $15M US exemption (2026) applies as anywhere".

claims.claim: The Temporary Retirement Visitor Visa from age 66 needs NZD 750,000 invested in New Zealand for 2 years, NZD 500,000 to live on, NZD 60,000 a year and insurance; 2 years at a time, renewable, never leading to residence

sources.name: Immigration New Zealand: Temporary Retirement Visitor Visa
sources.says: © 2026 (site notice 13 Nov 2026). "You must be 66 years or over"; "invest NZD $750,000 in acceptable investments in New Zealand for a minimum of 2 years"; "NZD $500,000 or more to live on"; "annual income of NZD $60,000 or more"; "maintain acceptable travel and/or health insurance"; stay up to 2 years, after which you "can apply for another Temporary Retirement Visitor Visa" if you still meet the requirements.

sources.name: Going NZ: retiring to New Zealand, the real visa options
sources.says: Updated July 2026. The Temporary Retirement Visitor Visa "is temporary. It does not lead to residence."

claims.note: INZ's page does not say whether it leads to residence; the "no residence" rests on Going NZ, which quotes INZ. Searched for a November 2026 change: none to this visa (family-visa lodging moves online on 16 November 2026).
